summary_of_pdf: This document is an RPost Registered Receipt serving as cryptographically verifiable proof of delivery, timestamp, and content for an electronic transmission sent by RJ Aguiar to attorneys at Hengeler Mueller. The underlying communication seeks intellectual property representation for a 47-patent portfolio while simultaneously disclosing highly sensitive parallel federal actions. The attachments indicate a complex, multi-front legal posture involving the US Department of Defense, Lockheed Martin, Goldman Sachs, SEC whistleblower retaliation claims (TCR 17742-648-351-976), formal criminal referrals against named individuals, and a DoD license grant involving Under Secretary Heidi Shyu.
attorneys_comments: From an evidentiary standpoint, this RPost receipt is a highly probative, self-authenticating business record under Federal Rules of Evidence 803(6) and 901, establishing undeniable actual notice to the recipient attorneys regarding the enclosed patent applications and explosive whistleblower allegations. Tactically, the sender is establishing a rigid paper trail of disclosures to prospective counsel, likely to preclude future claims of ignorance regarding the SEC whistleblower status or the alleged criminal conduct of the involved defense contractors. The inclusion of a DoD license grant suggests potential 28 U.S.C. § 1498 implications (eminent domain over patents by the federal government). However, the aggressive posture of bundling patent prosecution inquiries with formal criminal referrals and whistleblower retaliation claims presents a substantial liability and potential ethical conflict for any receiving counsel, as it intertwines standard 35 U.S.C. patent matters with volatile white-collar criminal allegations and procurement fraud.
recommended_next_steps: Immediately sequester this receipt and all native attachments in a secure, air-gapped evidentiary repository to preserve the chain of custody and metadata integrity. Conduct an exhaustive, firm-wide conflicts check regarding Goldman Sachs, Lockheed Martin, the US Department of Defense, and all named individuals (Herche, McDonald, Shyu). If representation is contemplated, bifurcate the patent prosecution matters from the whistleblower/criminal referral matters. Assess the DoD license grant under DFARS 227.7004 to determine the government's march-in rights or existing licenses, and evaluate potential jurisdiction in the United States Court of Federal Claims under 28 U.S.C. § 1498.
